# agents: clickable paths and image links

Branch `agents-panel`, worktree `/workspace/agents`, crate `agents/`. Read `agents/AGENTS.md` first.

## Goal

Every file path and attached-image placeholder the dashboard draws becomes a link: a plain left click on it runs macOS `open` on the target (files in their default app, directories in Finder). A click elsewhere on the same row keeps today's behavior.

## Shared representation (already committed, d0dada6)

- `crate::log::Image { label: String, path: PathBuf }` — an image attached to a prompt: its placeholder text in the prompt (e.g. `[Image #1]`) and its file.
- `Event.images: Vec<Image>` — images of a user-prompt log event.
- `Session.prompt_images: Vec<Image>` — images of `Session.prompt` (the prompt the details panel shows).

Providers fill these, and only with images whose file exists at load time. A placeholder with no entry draws as plain text. The UI never guesses image paths.

## Workstreams

### A. Claude provider (codex thread)

Real data (`~/.claude/projects/*/*.jsonl`): a prompt with an image is a `type:"user"` record whose text contains `[Image #N]` plus `{"type":"image","source":{"type":"base64",…}}` blocks; a separate companion record follows, `isMeta: true`, `turnCompanion: true`, whose `parentUuid` equals the prompt record's `uuid`, with text blocks `[Image: source: /workspace/tmp/<project>/<session>/images/N.png]` (one block per image). Real example: `~/.claude/projects/agents/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000.jsonl` lines 3410/3413 (two images) and 3028/3031.

1. Bug: the details prompt shows the companion's `[Image: source: …]` text instead of the user's prompt. `prompt_text` in `providers/claude/transcript.rs` does not skip `isMeta` records. Fix with a failing test first, fixture cut from the real records.
2. Fill `Session.prompt_images` from the companion of the record chosen as the prompt (join on `parentUuid` == `uuid`), and `Event.images` on the user events in `providers/claude/log.rs` (`walk_records` reads backward, so the companion arrives before its prompt: buffer by `parentUuid`). Pair each source with its `[Image #N]` label from the evidence in the data (e.g. order of blocks, or the `N` in `images/N.png`); check which holds on the real records. Keep only images whose file exists.
3. Look at the `last-prompt` record and `queued_command` attachments: if they carry `[Image #N]`, say whether paths are recoverable; do not invent them.

### B. Codex provider (codex thread)

Read `scratchpad/codex-images.md` (the research report on real rollouts). Summary: a user `response_item` message holds, per image, `input_text` `<image name=[Image #1] path="…">` (path optional), `input_image` (data URI), `input_text` `</image>`, then the user's text, which contains `[Image #1]`. The paired `event_msg`/`item_completed`/`UserMessage` carries `{"type":"local_image","path":…}` blocks. `Session.prompt` comes from SQLite `threads.first_user_message`, which already reads clean (`bug: [Image #1] …`), no path.

1. Bug: the task log shows the `<image …>` / `</image>` wrapper text verbatim. Strip the wrapper blocks in `providers/codex/rollout.rs`; failing test first, fixture from a real rollout.
2. Fill `Event.images` from the wrapper `path` attribute, falling back to the `UserMessage` event's `local_image.path` (check which order `tail()` sees them in). Keep only existing files.
3. A message with images but no user text is skipped today; when it has a wrapper `name`, show its `[Image #N]` labels instead.
4. Fill `Session.prompt_images` for the first user message, from the same rollout records. Keep it cheap: it is the first message of the rollout.

### C. UI (feature:ux-implementer)

Surfaces: the Project group header (`ui/rows.rs`), the details panel cwd line and its prompt / queued / activity / last-message bodies (`ui/render.rs`, `wrap_details`), the task log rows (`ui/log.rs` `fitted_body_line`), and the open log event view. Also move the existing PR link (`#123` in details) onto the same click mechanism, keeping its OSC 8.

1. Link targets: absolute paths, `~/` paths (expand home), relative paths like `a/b/c` resolved against the session's `cwd` and linked only when that file or directory exists (prose like `and/or` must stay plain). URLs stay plain. Tool rows use `Event.paths`; prose uses the existing `prose_path` detection, extended for relative paths. Image placeholders link to `Event.images` / `Session.prompt_images` targets.
2. The link always targets the full path even when the drawn text is abbreviated. `text_selection_layout.rs` already maps drawn columns back to source bytes through abbreviation; reuse that instead of a second map.
3. Draw links underlined. In-app click is the requirement; OSC 8 on paths is optional and `hyperlink()`'s `ForcedWidth(1)` is wrong for width-2 edge graphemes (`/界面/工具`).
4. Record link rects in the viewport like `details_copy` / `log_jump`; in `handle_mouse`, check them on a non-drag left Up before the log-row-opens-detail and copy branches. Add `Action::Open(PathBuf)` beside `Action::Copy` and run `open` detached where Copy is dispatched (macOS-only binary; guard with `cfg(target_os = "macos")` if needed).
5. Prompt and log rows show `[Image #N]`, never the image path.
6. Tests: buffer-level click tests in `ui/tests.rs` (see `task_log_click_opens_row_with_shortened_path`) for each surface: click on a link returns `Action::Open(full path)`, click elsewhere keeps today's behavior. Update `tests/ui_snapshots/` that move.

## Checks

`cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo build --release`, all in `agents/`.

input.prompt:
Write an implementation plan for a feature in the `agents` Rust TUI session dashboard, at /workspace/agents/agents (git worktree on branch `agents-panel`; read /workspace/agents/AGENTS.md and agents/AGENTS.md first). The plan will be run by the /feature:ship skill, so follow the format in /workspace/agents/plugins/feature/skills/ship/minimal-plan-template.md exactly (read SKILL.md in the same dir only for what the plan sections must contain). Write it to /workspace/tmp/agents/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000/scratchpad/plan.md and reply with the path plus a 5-line summary. Hard limit: 10 minutes; write partial output early and refine. Read only the lines you need.

## Feature: open a Tool log row to see its details

Today the task log (src/ui/log.rs `render_open_event`) can open User/Assistant/Agent rows: header row (time + kind label), blank row, then the body rendered as Markdown. Tool rows open too but just show `event.body` (one-line description). `Event` (src/log.rs) only stores `body`; tool inputs/outputs are discarded during parsing.

Goal: opening a Tool row (also Error/Denied rows that came from tool calls) shows, below the existing header, each tool call's **input** and, once the call has a result, its **output**. A running call (no result yet) shows input only.

Decided by the user:
- Both providers: Claude (src/providers/claude/log.rs `Log::tool` / result handling in `Log::record`) and Codex (src/providers/codex/rollout.rs, both `function_call`/`custom_tool_call` + `function_call_output` linked by call_id, and `event_msg item_completed` items like CommandExecution / FileChange).
- Input: Claude uses the `tool_use` block's `input`, never the record's `wireToolInputs`. Show extracted key fields, not raw JSON.
- Output: extracted key info, not the raw `toolUseResult` JSON. Claude result data lives in the user record's `tool_result` block (`content`, `is_error`) and `toolUseResult` (object for built-ins, e.g. Bash {stdout, stderr, interrupted, isImage, backgroundTaskId}; Write {filePath, content, ...}; WebFetch {url, code, result}; an array of {type:"text", text} content blocks for MCP tools, where `text` is often a JSON string). Images: skip for now.
- Per-tool extraction for the common tools: Bash (command highlighted as bash; stdout then stderr), Read (path + range; file content highlighted by extension — check whether toolUseResult carries raw content without the `N→` line-number prefix that tool_result content has, using a real transcript under ~/.claude/projects), Edit (path; old/new as a diff), Write (path; content by extension), Grep/Glob (key params; output text), WebFetch (url, prompt; result), Agent/SendMessage (prompt/message and reply as Markdown), MCP tools (args; text blocks, pretty-printed + highlighted when JSON). Codex: exec/exec_command/shell (command + output), apply_patch / FileChange (diff), others analogous.
- Every other tool: generic fallback — input as `key: value` lines, output as the tool_result text.
- Parallel calls in one assistant message are merged into ONE log row today (`Log::tool` batches them); the detail lists every call of that row, in order.
- Syntax highlighting like Codex's TUI: syntect + two-face (bat grammars). Use two-face/syntect with the pure-Rust `fancy` regex features (not onig). Guardrails as Codex: skip highlighting (plain text) above 512 KB, 10 000 lines, or any line over 4 KiB. Reference: Codex's implementation is saved at /workspace/tmp/agents/00000000-0000-4000-8000-000000000000/scratchpad/codex_highlight.rs (1688 lines; read only what you need, e.g. `highlight_code_to_lines`, `highlight_bash_to_lines`, the limits). Pick one bundled theme; the user will choose colors later from screenshots.
- Performance: `render_open_event` rebuilds lines every frame; highlighted output must be cached per opened event + width so scrolling a large output does not re-run syntect. Parsing cost is fine: walk_records already parses full records, only tens of rows are kept.
- Copying/text selection in the open view must keep working (see text_selection_layout::map_lines usage).

Constraints for the plan:
- Workstreams: backend data extraction (both providers + `Event` type + tests) goes to codex; the open-view rendering/highlighting (src/ui/*) is UX-changing frontend and goes to the `feature:ux-implementer` workstream. Define the shared data type up front in the plan so both can run in parallel.
- Tests use fixtures from one real upstream payload (copy real records from ~/.claude/projects/*.jsonl and ~/.codex/sessions/**.jsonl, trimmed); no mocks of behavior.
- Checks: per AGENTS.md (cargo test / clippy / fmt in agents/, whatever the repo's existing commands are — find them, e.g. package.json `test:agents` script or agents/AGENTS.md).
- UX verification: find the project's scripted probe for the log panel if one exists (grep for probe scripts under agents/ or tests/); state it in the plan, or say none exists.
- Keep it minimal; no line numbers; only what the implementer can't work out or would get wrong.

input.name: tool-calls
input.prompt:
Goal: in the `agents` Rust TUI (this repo's `agents/` dir; read AGENTS.md and agents/AGENTS.md first), the providers fill `Event.calls` with each tool call's extracted input and output sections, so the UI (built by another workstream in parallel) can show them when a Tool log row is opened. Another workstream edits src/ui/* in its own worktree; never touch those files.

### `tool-calls` — providers fill `Event.calls` for every tool row

1. Claude results: `ResultAt` in `Log` keeps the `tool_result` block's `content` (string, or the
   joined `text` blocks) and the record's `toolUseResult` `Value` next to `at`/`error`/`denial`,
   because `walk_records` walks backwards and the result record is seen before its `tool_use` —
   `Log::record` `agents/src/providers/claude/log.rs`.
2. Claude extraction: `Log::tool` builds one `ToolCall` from the `tool_use` block's `input` (never
   `wireToolInputs`) and the kept result, and splices it at index 0 of `entry.event.calls`, the
   same way the body is prepended, so calls stay in file order — new `fn tool_call(name, input,
   result: Option<&ResultAt>) -> ToolCall` in the same file.
   Per tool (fallback for anything else: input `Fields` of every input key as `key: value`,
   non-string values compact JSON; output `Text` of the tool_result content):
   - Bash: input `Code{bash}` of `command` plus `Fields` description when present; output
     `Text stdout` then `Text stderr` from `toolUseResult.stdout/stderr` (omit empty ones);
     without `toolUseResult`, `Text` of the tool_result content.
   - Read: `Fields` path and range (`offset`/`limit` → "lines A–B"); output `Code` of
     `toolUseResult.file.content` (raw text, no `N→` prefix: verified in a real transcript) with
     `lang` = the path's extension; range label from `file.startLine`/`numLines`; without
     `toolUseResult.file` (error), `Text` of the tool_result content.
   - Edit: `Fields` path; input `Diff` from `toolUseResult.structuredPatch` hunks when present
     (`oldStart`,`oldLines`,`newStart`,`newLines`,`lines`: rebuild `@@ -a,b +c,d @@` + lines),
